labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE: FS-UAE 3.2.35 (its OWN copy at assets/amix/fsuae-native, built with FSUAE_STATION=amix) runs an Amiga 3000 (68030+MMU, Kickstart 2.04 r37.175) on the host inside a pinned Xvfb sized to the emulator window; the daemon captures the X root (SH_CAPTURE=x11) and injects input over XTEST. No QEMU/QMP, no exec channel. POINTER: ABSOLUTE via the GUEST's X server (SH_X11TEST_MOTION=warp + SH_X11WARP_DISPLAY=127.0.0.1:72). The UAE mousehack is an AmigaOS trap AMIX never registers, so XTEST motion is relative+accelerated there; instead the A2065 runs on slirp and the launcher's patched FS-UAE (fsuae-slirp-hostfwd.patch) adds a LOOPBACK-ONLY redirect 127.0.0.1:6072 -> 10.0.2.15:6000 to the guest's X11R4 server; the daemon warps (XWarpPointer) and reads back (XQueryPointer); buttons/keys ride XTEST into the Xvfb with the edge held until the warp is confirmed. Single injector: never push motion at this guest by another path (no xdotool mousemove on the live Xvfb). The pointer is dead while the guest X server is (boot ~2 min; the launcher's x11warp-check.log says ok / STALE GOLDEN / TIMED OUT). Golden carries /etc/inet/hosts (amix=10.0.2.15, slirphost=10.0.2.2, no default route) and xhost +slirphost in /etc/kh-xsession. Reset=relaunch: cold boot (~2 min) of a fresh work HDF copied from disk/amix-system.hdf.golden; no statefile. The launcher also pins --zoom=640x512: FS-UAE's default 692x540 crop draws the X root at 0.925/0.948 scale and the pointer is 1:1 only with the pinned crop. Framebuffer-proven 2026-09-01: readback exact and sprite tip on target at 16 points incl. all four corners, residual 0 px (docs/guests/amix.md). Launcher stations/amix/x11-runtime.sh.

render.stationsManifestPrelude: # amix — host-native FS-UAE 3.2.35 (A3000, 68030+MMU, Kickstart 2.04) -> Amiga UNIX (AMIX) 2.1, System V R4 with the OPEN LOOK desktop, in COLOUR on an A2410 (1024x768, 8-bit PseudoColor, selected by starting AMIX's X server with -tiga). The chipset X server is depth 1, so monochrome 640x512 is the fallback and is one flag away (/etc/kh-xsession.mono in the guest). Absolute 1:1 pointer via x11warp into the guest's own X server over a loopback-bound slirp redirect.

museum.lineage: Commodore Amiga / AT&T UNIX System V Release 4 (ported by Commodore)
museum.arch: Motorola 68030 @ 25 MHz with MMU + 68882 FPU, A2410 graphics board (Amiga 3000)
eraSoftware: X11R4 and the AT&T OPEN LOOK toolkit (OLIT)
museum.periodBrowser: none — this station is offline, and in 1992 a Unix machine's network was uucp and Usenet: AMIX ships C News, NNTP and an SVR4 TCP/IP stack, not a browser
museum.blurb: Commodore licensed AT&T's System V Release 4 and shipped it on the Amiga 3000, wearing OPEN LOOK — the desktop AT&T specified for SVR4, and the one Motif beat — instead of Workbench. Nobody ever published how many sold. This one has the A2410 graphics board fitted, so it runs OPEN LOOK in colour: the option that took the price from $4,998 to $7,713.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile, HOST-NATIVE from birth: FS-UAE 3.2.35 on the host under a pinned Xvfb, x11 root capture + XTEST input, with its own copy of the binary (rule 6). Installed from real media — the AMIX 2.1 boot/root floppies and the 29-segment installation tape (amigaunix.com) restored through UAE's SCSI tape emulation onto a 2 GB RDB disk, exactly as a real A3000UX did it. SHIPS IN COLOUR: the pinned FS-UAE build does drive the Commodore A2410, and AMIX's X server comes up on it at 1024x768 depth 8 PseudoColor (256 colours) when started with -tiga — /usr/X/bin/X and /usr/X/bin/X2410 are byte-identical, so the board is selected by that flag alone. The earlier 'FS-UAE compiles the A2410 code but never calls it' verdict was a tool artefact: ugrep skipped the ISO-8859 gfxboard.cpp as binary, and the dispatch functions are named tms_*, not a2410_*. The 640x512 depth-1 chipset session is kept in-guest as /etc/kh-xsession.mono, so monochrome is a one-line revert. Historically the A2410 was a $998 option and most A3000UX owners ran the mono chipset screen; the poster says so. Distinct from amiga (A500/WB1.3), amigaos35 (A4000/OS 3.5) and aros. See docs/guests/amix.md.

network.note: A2065 on FS-UAE slirp, used ONLY for the pointer: a loopback-bound redirect 127.0.0.1:6072 -> guest 10.0.2.15:6000 lets the daemon drive the guest's X server. Fail-closed: the guest has no default route (only 10.0.2.0/24), the redirect binds 127.0.0.1, and there is no retronet tap. Not a retronet join; a web-plane join remains a follow-up.

reset.mouse: PASS (2026-09-01) — ABSOLUTE through the guest's own X11R4 server: SH_X11TEST_MOTION=warp warps with XWarpPointer and reads back with XQueryPointer over the launcher's loopback-only slirp redirect 127.0.0.1:6072 -> 10.0.2.15:6000; buttons/keys stay on XTEST and a button edge waits for the confirmed warp. Framebuffer-proven sweep in docs/guests/amix.md.
reset.fixture: AMIX 2.1 OPEN LOOK desktop on a 640x512 monochrome screen: an xterm titled 'Amiga UNIX 2.1' showing 'UNIX_System_V amix 4.0 2.1 0800430 Amiga (Unlimited) m68k' over a root shell, xcalc (in its TI-30 layout, wearing OPEN LOOK's rounded buttons rather than the square Athena ones), and xclock. Started from /etc/inittab (entry 'xw', run level 2) via xinit /etc/kh-xsession, so the desktop is up without a login. resetMode=relaunch with no statefile: reset is a COLD BOOT (~2 min to the desktop) of a fresh work HDF copied from disk/amix-system.hdf.golden. BAKE RULE: halt the guest with /sbin/shutdown -y -g0 -i0 before copying the golden — UFS has no host-repairable dirty flag, and a golden taken from a killed emulator makes every visitor's boot run a full fsck (~4 min instead of ~2). Keyboard PASS on the sandbox rig 2026-08-30 (XTEST). Mouse OPEN: motion reaches the guest but is relative and accelerated.
